chapter_theme: Reviling the Lord's devotees (மயேசுர நிந்தை): the devotees stand apart from everyone and live on alms, and those who speak ill of them fall into low hell; when a jnani is reviled or worshipped, the deeds are divided and he enters Siva's bliss.

537.reading: The Lord's devotees are at odds with everyone; the Lord's devotees eat what they receive as alms; those who speak unwanted words of the Lord's devotees fall, each of them, into low hell.
537.nuance: ஆர்க்கும் விரோதிகள் (opponents of all) is taken as their standing apart from worldly ways, not as hostility; it may also be read with a negative understood, 'enemies to none'. The repeated ஆண்டான் அடியவர் opens three lines.

538.reading: The one who reviles the jnani and the one who worships the jnani as good take away his good and his cruel deeds; the moment he has passed into the Lord's keeping, Siva's bliss enters.
538.nuance: This is the traditional reading: the worshipper takes the jnani's good deeds and the reviler his bad ones, leaving him free of both. The verse runs the two together (நல்வினையான கொடுவினை), so which goes to whom is inferred, not stated.

links.note: 534 threatens land, kings and Indra's throne when devotees are troubled; 537 sends those who speak ill of them to low hell. One names the public ruin, the other the personal one.
